00001| # Proprietary Software Scanner for Linux
00002| 
00003| A command-line tool that scans Linux systems for proprietary software, helping users identify and track non-free software on their systems.
00004| 
00005| ## Features
00006| 
00007| - **Package Manager Integration**: Automatically detects and scans packages from major Linux package managers (apt, dnf/yum, pacman, rpm, zypper, emerge, xbps)
00008| - **Filesystem Scanning**: Scans executable files for proprietary indicators
00009| - **Multiple Output Formats**: Supports table, JSON, and CSV output formats
00010| - **Configuration Support**: Customizable scanning parameters via JSON configuration file
00011| - **Comprehensive Database**: Built-in database of known proprietary software packages
00012| 
00013| ## Installation
00014| 
00015| 1. Download the script:
00016| 
00017|    ```bash
00018|    wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yourusername/proprietary-scanner/main/proprietary-scanner.py
00019|    ```
00020| 
00021| 2. Make it executable:
00022| 
00023|    ```bash
00024|    chmod +x proprietary-scanner.py
00025|    ```
00026| 
00027| 3. (Optional) Install required dependencies:
00028| 
00029|    ```bash
00030|    # For Debian/Ubuntu
00031|    sudo apt install python3
00032| 
00033|    # For RHEL/CentOS/Fedora
00034|    sudo dnf install python3
00035| 
00036|    # For Arch Linux
00037|    sudo pacman -S python
00038|    ```
00039| 
00040| ## Usage
00041| 
00042| ### Basic Usage
00043| 
00044| Scan installed packages only:
00045| 
00046| ```bash
00047| ./proprietary-scanner.py
00048| ```
00049| 
00050| Scan both packages and filesystem:
00051| 
00052| ```bash
00053| ./proprietary-scanner.py --filesystem
00054| ```
00055| 
00056| ### Advanced Usage
00057| 
00058| Scan specific directories:
00059| 
00060| ```bash
00061| ./proprietary-scanner.py --filesystem --dirs /usr/bin /opt /home/user/bin
00062| ```
00063| 
00064| Output in JSON format:
00065| 
00066| ```bash
00067| ./proprietary-scanner.py --output json
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| Save results to CSV file:
00071| 
00072| ```bash
00073| ./proprietary-scanner.py --output csv > results.csv
00074| ```
00075| 
00076| Use custom configuration file:
00077| 
00078| ```bash
00079| ./proprietary-scanner.py --config my-config.json
00080| ```
00081| 
00082| Enable verbose output:
00083| 
00084| ```bash
00085| ./proprietary-scanner.py --verbose
00086| ```
00087| 
00088| ### Command Line Options
00089| 
00090| | Option         | Short | Description                                                       |
00091| | -------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
00092| | `--filesystem` | `-f`  | Scan filesystem for proprietary binaries                          |
00093| | `--dirs`       | `-d`  | Directories to scan (default: /usr/bin /usr/local/bin /opt /home) |
00094| | `--output`     | `-o`  | Output format: table, json, csv (default: table)                  |
00095| | `--config`     | `-c`  | Configuration file path (default: config.json)                    |
00096| | `--verbose`    | `-v`  | Enable verbose output                                             |
00097| | `--help`       | `-h`  | Show help message                                                 |
00098| 
00099| ## Configuration
00100| 
00101| The tool supports configuration via JSON file. By default, it looks for `config.json` in the current directory.
00102| 
00103| ### Example Configuration
00104| 
00105| ```json
00106| {
00107|   "scan_directories": ["/usr/bin", "/usr/local/bin", "/opt", "/home"],
00108|   "exclude_directories": ["/proc", "/sys", "/dev", "/tmp"],
00109|   "proprietary_keywords": [
00110|     "proprietary",
00111|     "commercial",
00112|     "closed-source",
00113|     "license",
00114|     "trial",
00115|     "demo",
00116|     "shareware",
00117|     "freemium"
00118|   ],
00119|   "proprietary_companies": [
00120|     "microsoft",
00121|     "google",
00122|     "adobe",
00123|     "oracle",
00124|     "apple",
00125|     "amazon",
00126|     "facebook",
00127|     "meta",
00128|     "nvidia",
00129|     "amd",
00130|     "intel",
00131|     "vmware",
00132|     "autodesk",
00133|     "mathworks",
00134|     "wolfram",
00135|     "spotify",
00136|     "slack",
00137|     "dropbox",
00138|     "teamviewer",
00139|     "zoom",
00140|     "skype",
00141|     "discord"
00142|   ],
00143|   "known_proprietary_packages": {
00144|     "google-chrome-stable": "proprietary",
00145|     "slack-desktop": "proprietary",
00146|     "teamviewer": "proprietary",
00147|     "zoom": "proprietary",
00148|     "skypeforlinux": "proprietary",
00149|     "spotify-client": "proprietary",
00150|     "discord": "proprietary",
00151|     "steam": "proprietary",
00152|     "microsoft-edge-stable": "proprietary",
00153|     "vscode": "proprietary"
00154|   },
00155|   "output_format": "table",
00156|   "verbose": false
00157| }
00158| ```
00159| 
00160| ### Configuration Options
00161| 
00162| - **scan_directories**: List of directories to scan for proprietary binaries
00163| - **exclude_directories**: List of directories to exclude from filesystem scanning
00164| - **proprietary_keywords**: Keywords that indicate proprietary software in package names
00165| - **proprietary_companies**: Company names that indicate proprietary software
00166| - **known_proprietary_packages**: Dictionary of known proprietary package names (includes traditional and Flatpak package IDs)
00167| - **output_format**: Default output format (table, json, csv)
00168| - **verbose**: Enable verbose output by default
00169| 
00170| ## Output Formats
00171| 
00172| ### Table Format (Default)
00173| 
00174| ```
00175| Name                Version      License      Source        Path/Package Manager
00176| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
00177| google-chrome-stable 115.0.5790.102 proprietary package_manager apt
00178| slack-desktop        4.29.149     proprietary package_manager apt
00179| zoom                5.15.5.21073 proprietary package_manager apt
00180| ```
00181| 
00182| ### JSON Format
00183| 
00184| ```json
00185| [
00186|   {
00187|     "name": "google-chrome-stable",
00188|     "version": "115.0.5790.102",
00189|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00190|     "source": "package_manager",
00191|     "path": null,
00192|     "package_manager": "apt"
00193|   },
00194|   {
00195|     "name": "slack-desktop",
00196|     "version": "4.29.149",
00197|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00198|     "source": "package_manager",
00199|     "path": null,
00200|     "package_manager": "apt"
00201|   }
00202| ]
00203| ```
00204| 
00205| ### CSV Format
00206| 
00207| ```csv
00208| name,version,license_type,source,path,package_manager
00209| google-chrome-stable,115.0.5790.102,proprietary,package_manager,,apt
00210| slack-desktop,4.29.149,proprietary,package_manager,,apt
00211| ```
00212| 
00213| ## Examples
00214| 
00215| ### Example 1: Basic Package Scan
00216| 
00217| ```bash
00218| $ ./proprietary-scanner.py
00219| Detected package manager: apt
00220| Scanning for proprietary software...
00221| Found 3 proprietary software items
00222| Name                Version      License      Source        Path/Package Manager
00223| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
00224| google-chrome-stable 115.0.5790.102 proprietary package_manager apt
00225| slack-desktop        4.29.149     proprietary package_manager apt
00226| zoom                5.15.5.21073 proprietary package_manager apt
00227| ```
00228| 
00229| ### Example 2: Full System Scan with JSON Output
00230| 
00231| ```bash
00232| $ ./proprietary-scanner.py --filesystem --output json --verbose
00233| Detected package manager: apt
00234| Scanning for proprietary software...
00235| Found 5 proprietary software items
00236| [
00237|   {
00238|     "name": "google-chrome-stable",
00239|     "version": "115.0.5790.102",
00240|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00241|     "source": "package_manager",
00242|     "path": null,
00243|     "package_manager": "apt"
00244|   },
00245|   {
00246|     "name": "slack-desktop",
00247|     "version": "4.29.149",
00248|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00249|     "source": "package_manager",
00250|     "path": null,
00251|     "package_manager": "apt"
00252|   },
00253|   {
00254|     "name": "zoom",
00255|     "version": "5.15.5.21073",
00256|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00257|     "source": "package_manager",
00258|     "path": null,
00259|     "package_manager": "apt"
00260|   },
00261|   {
00262|     "name": "chrome",
00263|     "version": "",
00264|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00265|     "source": "file_system",
00266|     "path": "/opt/google/chrome/chrome"
00267|   },
00268|   {
00269|     "name": "slack",
00270|     "version": "",
00271|     "license_type": "proprietary",
00272|     "source": "file_system",
00273|     "path": "/usr/bin/slack"
00274|   }
00275| ]
00276| ```
00277| 
00278| ### Example 3: Custom Configuration
00279| 
00280| ```bash
00281| $ ./proprietary-scanner.py --config custom-config.json --filesystem --dirs /usr/bin /opt
00282| ```
00283| 
00284| ## Requirements
00285| 
00286| - Python 3.6 or higher
00287| - Linux system with one of the supported package managers:
00288|   - apt/dpkg (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint)
00289|   - dnf/yum/rpm (Fedora, CentOS, RHEL)
00290|   - pacman (Arch Linux)
00291|   - zypper (openSUSE)
00292|   - emerge (Gentoo)
00293|   - xbps (Void Linux)
00294|   - flatpak (universal package manager)
00295| 
00296| - For filesystem scanning:
00297|   - `file` command (usually pre-installed)
00298|   - `strings` command (usually pre-installed)
00299|   - Root privileges recommended for full filesystem access
00300| 
00301| ## Limitations
00302| 
00303| - The tool relies on package names and maintainer information to determine license type
00304| - Some proprietary software may not be detected if it doesn't match the known patterns
00305| - Filesystem scanning requires appropriate permissions to access all directories
00306| - The tool may produce false positives or false negatives
00307| - Flatpak applications may have different naming conventions (application IDs vs traditional package names)
00308| - Some Flatpak applications may be sandboxed and not fully accessible during filesystem scanning
00309| 
00310| ## Contributing
00311| 
00312| Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit issues and pull requests.
00313| 
00314| ### Adding New Proprietary Packages
00315| 
00316| To add new proprietary packages to the database, edit the `known_proprietary_packages` section in the configuration file:
00317| 
00318| ```json
00319| {
00320|   "known_proprietary_packages": {
00321|     "existing-package": "proprietary",
00322|     "new-proprietary-package": "proprietary",
00323|     "com.example.NewApp": "proprietary"
00324|   }
00325| }
00326| ```
00327| 
00328| **Note:** For Flatpak packages, use the full application ID (e.g., `com.google.Chrome` instead of just `chrome`).
00329| 
00330| ### Adding New Proprietary Companies
00331| 
00332| To add new companies to the detection list, edit the `proprietary_companies` section:
00333| 
00334| ```json
00335| {
00336|   "proprietary_companies": ["existing-company", "new-company"]
00337| }
00338| ```
00339| 
00340| ## License
00341| 
00342| This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the LICENSE file for details.
00343| 
00344| ## Disclaimer
00345| 
00346| This tool is provided as-is for educational and informational purposes. The detection of proprietary software is based on heuristics and may not be 100% accurate. Always verify the license status of software through official sources.
00347|
